  return a + b

  b.wait()
  g(77)

  for _ in range(10000):
    b = threading.Barrier(num_threads)
    g = functools.partial(f, a=42)

`partial_vectorcall_fallback` sets `vectorcall` to nullptr if it decides to fall back to a non-vectorcall code path:
https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/b92f101d0f19a1df32050b8502cfcce777b079b2/Modules/_functoolsmodule.c#L366

But this races with the code that reads an object's `vectorcall` in the core function call code: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/b92f101d0f19a1df32050b8502cfcce777b079b2/Include/internal/pycore_call.h#L128

comments.body: Looks like a race. Probably somewhat related to #127266, but this isn't a full type slot, it's an offset.

Here perhaps the best fix is to implement the missing vectorcall case in `partial`?

(Or just skip setting the pointer to nullptr in free-threading mode.)

It seems like a fairly benign race: all it does is prevent a fast-path from being taken again. But there's no such thing as a benign race.

I think we should set `vectorcall` once in the partial constructor, instead of sometimes setting it to NULL lazily when it's invoked. 

I don't think there's a good enough reason to have a different implementation for the default build and free threading build. I don't think this sort of change will have any performance impact.

This one is waiting for review https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/124584

It eliminates dynamic switching as `vectorcall` can handle all cases.

This happens sometimes on CI https://github.com/python/cpython/actions/runs/16065399445/job/45338930486, I think we should add suppression for this until this is fixed on both main and older branches, it is unlikely that it will be fixed for 3.13 now.

I think I'm intermittently getting this race reported by TSAN in [my CI](https://github.com/dpdani/cereggii/actions/runs/20644092207/job/59279624375?pr=108).
